principles: Fail closed: no production-capable key and proof endpoint means no production smoke pass.
Host-neutral evidence: Claude and Codex can review, but Authority receipts remain the authority source.
Narrow scope: target TEST gate only and avoid DONE semantics or unrelated refactors.
Structured anchors over prose: record ids, digests, commits, and classifications.
Do not optimize arbitrarily; only react to correctness blockers found by the smoke.
drivers: Staging currently appears reachable but production-inert and missing the proof endpoint.
The release rule forbids claiming production readiness from local-test or contract-only evidence.
The worktree must stay isolated from the eight unrelated dirty files on Orchestrate main.

options.name: readiness-first-fail-closed-smoke
pros: Stops before mutating positive flow when staging cannot produce production evidence.
Produces an honest formal BLOCKED transcript with exact environment/version blockers.
Matches the documented release rule and host-neutral trust boundary.
cons: If staging is not deployed/configured correctly, this story ends as blocked/audit evidence rather than a green E2E pass.

options.name: attempt-full-positive-flow-anyway
pros: Could exercise more endpoints if credentials and server behavior happen to allow it.
cons: Risks treating local-test or transport-only results as authority evidence.
Would spend effort on mutating calls even after readiness already proves the smoke cannot be production-valid.

options.name: fallback-to-local-stub
cons: Does not answer the user request for formal staging verification.
Would duplicate prior contract/stub coverage and violate the live smoke release rule.

rationale: Choose readiness-first fail-closed smoke because the user asked for formal staging verification and our docs require production-capable authority before any TEST gate receipt can count. If staging readiness fails, the correct deliverable is a structured BLOCKED classification, not a forced green path.

preMortem.scenario: Staging is reachable but still advertises dev-server-key/local-test/productionInert.
preMortem.trigger: GET /v1/authority/policy shows productionInert=true or default/dev key id.
preMortem.consequence: A positive smoke would be invalid and misleading.
preMortem.mitigation: Stop at CHK-001, record invalid production authority blocker, do not write production-gate-decision receipt refs.

preMortem.scenario: Staging has not deployed the receipt proof endpoint.
preMortem.consequence: CLI cannot verify inputDigest/decisionDigest proof bundle for gate consumption.
preMortem.mitigation: Classify as environment version blocker and do not claim receipt verification.

preMortem.scenario: Secrets or identities are missing in the local environment.
preMortem.trigger: API key, actor key, runner id, session id, project id, or trusted pin source is absent.
preMortem.consequence: Mutating live flow cannot safely run or would expose secrets if mishandled.
preMortem.mitigation: Record only presence/absence, never secret values, and stop before positive flow.

preMortem.scenario: Host evidence is confused with Authority evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Claude/Codex agree on transcript but no verified production receipt exists.
preMortem.consequence: User could believe production readiness was proven when it was not.
preMortem.mitigation: State host verdicts are local evidence only and require production gate_decision receipt for PASS.
